title: This $39 touchscreen packs a powerful new ESP32 chip with Wi-Fi 6, Zigbee, and Thread
excerpt: A feature-packed module offers dual-core RISC-V performance, 16MB PSRAM, RS485 and CAN interfaces, and an 800x480 capacitive touchscreen.

Published Oct 14, 2026, 9:37 AM EDT

Hamed holds a B.A. in English Literature, graduating cum laude. He loves music, tech gadgets, and exploring the latest in the world of LLMs. He also enjoys tinkering with creative software such as Logic Pro, Final Cut Pro, and Photoshop.

A lifelong musician, Hamed plays multiple instruments, including guitar, bass, and oud. He is equally fascinated by smart-home technology and can happily spend hours geeking out over connected lights, speakers, sensors, and automations that make everyday life a little more interesting. When he isn’t covering the latest tech news, he explores more creative topics on his Medium blog, works on his music, or clears his head by riding his motorcycle.

If you're into DIY tech projects, Espressif's newly released ESP32-S31 platform has definitely been on your radar. Now, VIEWE has launched a $38.99 touchscreen development board built around it that packs plenty of features into one compact unit.

According to the company’s official product page, the UES31S043H800V480C-U combines a 4.3-inch capacitive display with Wi-Fi 6, Bluetooth 5.4, and an IEEE 802.15.4 radio capable of supporting Zigbee and Thread. The board uses the ESP32-S31-WROOM-3-N16R16V module, which contains the ESP32-S31NRV16 system-on-chip.

An ESP32-and-touchscreen combo you can't miss

One that's significantly more affordable than Raspberry Pi 5

In our closer look at the new ESP32-S31, we explored how this generation adds several notable features beyond faster processing, including wireless hardware that supports 2.4GHz Wi-Fi 6 at up to 150Mbps, Bluetooth 5.4 LE, Bluetooth Classic, and IEEE 802.15.4 for Zigbee and Thread.

Thanks to global RAM shortages, the spike in Raspberry Pi 5 prices has pushed the boards beyond what many of us would comfortably spend. That sub-$40 price looks even more convincing when you consider VIEWE’s feature-rich development board.

VIEWE’s board comes with an IPS panel featuring an 800 x 480 resolution, 400-nit brightness, and a GT911 capacitive touch controller. Moreover, you get a USB-C port for power, programming, and debugging, alongside a separate USB-A port with USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG. You can find a list of the specifications and features in the table below:

Feature

Specification

Processor

ESP32-S31NRV16 dual-core RISC-V SoC, up to 320MHz

Wireless module

ESP32-S31-WROOM-3-N16R16V

Memory

16MB flash and 16MB PSRAM

Display

4.3-inch IPS, 800x480 resolution, 400-nit brightness

Touch input

GT911 capacitive touchscreen

Wi-Fi

2.4GHz Wi-Fi 6, up to 150Mbps

Other wireless

Bluetooth 5.4 LE, Bluetooth Classic, Zigbee, and Thread

USB

USB-C for power and programming; USB-A with USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG

Storage and expansion

MicroSD slot with four-bit SDMMC and 20-pin GPIO header

Industrial interfaces

RS485 and CAN

Audio

ES8389 stereo codec, two amplifiers, and dual microphones

Software support

ESP-IDF, LVGL, and 18 example projects; Arduino support in development

Zigbee and Thread make it a solid device for DIY smart home kits since many lights, plugs, and sensors work better on those mesh protocols than on Wi-Fi. However, all the board’s wireless standards share one 2.4GHz radio. Espressif recommends using two chips with separate antennas for a more reliable Thread border router or Zigbee gateway.
